judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 1 (rank 1) Skills about oral narrative production. The first SFI sits in the later Term 4, Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities ('Tells a familiar story which has a beginning, middle and end, varying tone and volume of voice'), decomposed into LCs for explicit story structure (beginning, middle, end) and for varying tone and volume. The later statement adds narrative-structure control and expressive delivery to the earlier picture-supported, unstructured story-making, so proficiency in constructing a story from pictures plausibly supports success in telling a structured, expressively delivered story. Direction therefore runs from the earlier Term 2 statement to the later Term 4 statement (second_to_first), consistent with the within-grade Term 1-to-4 ordering. Confidence is moderate because the two statements fall in different Skill Areas, lexical overlap is low (shared token 'story' only), and both endpoints' source evidence (and the second's LC evidence) is truncated, so the full printed context could not be inspected.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 1, Term 2, Reading and Phonics, under the 'Daily Phonemic Awareness/ Phonic Activities' sub-strand (same Grade rank 1, same Term, so a same-term developmental direction requires substantive evidence). Meaningful reinforcement without justified developmental dependency therefore yields the symmetric relatesTo with null direction and canonical endpoint order unchanged. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 2 (rank 2) Skills under the READING AND PHONICS skill area, but in different terms and sub-strands: the first is Term 2 Phonics ('Recognises ‘silent e’/split digraph in words, e.g. tape, time, note'), the second is Term 1 Group Guided Reading ('Reads both silently and aloud at own level in a Guided Reading group with teacher'). A buildsTowards first_to_second would run Term 2 back to Term 1 within the same grade and is therefore invalid; the forward second_to_first direction is not substantively supported either, since reading at one's instructional level in a guided group is not evidence that it develops the specific split-digraph grapheme knowledge, nor is the phonics item a stated extension of guided reading. The nomination's strongest lexical trigger ('silent', 'sil'/'len' trigrams) is a false friend between 'silent e' and 'reads silently', so it carries no semantic weight. What does justify a symmetric link is genuine instructional complementarity within the same CAPS reading programme: word-level decoding of split-digraph words and applying decoding while reading connected text at own level reinforce one another without an evidenced dependency. Both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, coordinates and LC tags supplied.

The shared parent Skill Area and page/rank proximity alone are not decisive, and the token/trigram overlap is only function words ('a', 'in', 'the'), so the judgment rests on substantive content: secure word-level decoding of common initial digraphs (LC tags: digraphs, initial sounds, phonics) directly supports accurate oral reading of connected text from an own book in a guided group (LC tags: guided reading, reading aloud). Same-Term direction is permitted and is justified here by the word-level-to-text-level component relationship, not by repeated wording; the text-level reading task does not conversely presuppose digraph revision. Confidence is moderated because both statements are same-term, the phonics item is framed as revision, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so fuller source text could refine the reading.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading. The second SFI is Grade R Term 2, Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness': 'Distinguishes aurally between different sounds especially at the beginning of words' (LC tags: beginning sounds, listening, phonemic awareness). The first SFI is Grade R Term 3, Sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words': 'Recognises aurally and visually some initial consonants and vowels especially at the beginning of common words', with the Helen/'h' example (LC tags: consonants, initial sounds, letter-sound, phonics, vowels). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 3 statement extends purely aural discrimination of beginning sounds into combined aural-and-visual identification of specific initial consonants and vowels mapped to printed letters. Proficiency in aurally distinguishing initial sounds supports success in attaching those initial sounds to letters, so the earlier Term 2 skill builds towards the later Term 3 skill (second_to_first, a permitted earlier-to-later direction within Grade R). Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), but the retained statement text, identity scopes and LCs are sufficient and non-contradictory.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 3, Term 4, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics' (same coordinate rank 3, same Term node), but under different printed sub-strands: 'Shared Reading' (reads written texts as a whole class with the teacher and discusses characters, the 'problem', plot and values) versus 'Group Guided Reading' (uses self-correcting strategies when reading: reading, pausing, practising a word before saying it aloud). The first is text-level comprehension and response within teacher-led whole-class reading; the second is word-level monitoring and self-correction during guided reading. They are complementary components of the same term's reading programme and mutually reinforcing, but the evidence shows no substantive expansion of one into the other and no basis for asserting that proficiency in either specifically supports success in the other; same-Grade, same-Term placement alone cannot supply developmental direction, and the shared 'reading' token/page-proximity signals are weak. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this rests on the bounded excerpts.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading Skills about applying word-recognition strategies while reading, but they sit in different terms of the same grade: the second SFI is Term 2 ('Uses phonics, context clues and sight words when reading') and the first is Term 3 ('Uses phonics, context clues, and structural analysis and sight words when reading'). The later Term 3 statement retains the Term 2 strategy set and adds structural analysis, a substantive expansion of the decoding toolkit rather than mere repeated wording; LC tags confirm the added 'structural analysis' component in the Term 3 node only. Proficiency with the Term 2 phonics/context-clue/sight-word strategies supports success with the extended Term 3 set, so the permitted direction is earlier term to later term (second_to_first), consistent with the within-grade Term 1-to-4 ordering rule. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, identity-scope terms, and LC tags.
